stem.en: Kabir says "water is a conductor, that is why wet hands are dangerous." What does the six-glass test actually show?

text.en: Pure water is not a conductor. Wet hands are dangerous because sweat and tap water carry dissolved salts, which make them a weak electrolyte.

feedback.en: Distilled water gave nothing at all. The conducting is done by what is dissolved, not by the water.

text.en: Water conducts only when it is cold.

feedback.en: Temperature was never a dial in this test. Salt was. Warm salt water conducts as well as cold.
Nimbu pani glowed too, and tap water glowed faintly. Anything with the right kind of dissolved stuff conducts a little.

explanation.en: Look at what the six glasses have in common. Every one that glowed had something dissolved in it that came from a salt or an acid. Every one that stayed dark either had nothing dissolved or had sugar or oil.
